faq.a: Enamel is the hard, shiny outer layer of the tooth crown. It is about 96 percent mineral, mainly a calcium phosphate called hydroxyapatite, making it the hardest substance in the human body.
asks: What is the hardest part of the body?

faq.a: Dentine is the layer under the enamel and makes up most of the tooth. It is softer than enamel, slightly yellow, and full of microscopic tubes that connect to the pulp.

faq.q: What is in the pulp of a tooth?
faq.a: The pulp is the soft core of the tooth. It contains nerves, blood vessels and cells that make dentine, and it keeps the tooth alive.
If dentine is exposed, temperature changes make fluid move inside its tiny tubes, which stimulates nerves in the pulp. Your brain reads that as a sharp feeling.
asks: Why do my teeth tingle with ice cream?

faq.q: How are teeth held in the jaw?
faq.a: Each root sits in a socket in the jawbone, held by a sling of tiny fibres called the periodontal ligament, attached to the cementum on the root. It lets the tooth move very slightly when you bite.

facts: Tooth enamel is about 96 percent mineral by weight and is the hardest substance in the human body.
Enamel has no living cells, so the body cannot regrow it.
